proof.negativeControl: applyMargin recording content_changed=true; skipping its anchor refresh; reusing a rendering taken before its own forkLive: each failed the test with a named mismatch.

trickyParts: applyMargin reuses liveWrite.tree only after its own forkLive: buildFork/releaseFork/abandon drop the rendering whenever the fork moves.

The observer skip is limited to a margin write whose fork was warm-built from the very room instance the update is applied to; ygo encodes every update with its document's whole delete set, so a cold fork's margin update can delete text the room still holds (TestAMarginWriteFromAColdForkIsRenderedByTheRoomItIsPublishedInto).

refreshAnchors is called unconditionally from recordLiveOperation (writeVersionTx with a nil write), not through the anchorsTree guard: on an anchored root it is the first refresh that sees the new comment row.
deviations: Measured gain 0.032 cores at F=0.3 against the plan's expected ~0.084; the rule's first condition (every head < every base) holds. The observer share did not move: in the replay rooms are mostly evicted between writes (roomIdleTimeout one minute, CLI-only load), so margin writes fork cold and are not tagged [INFERENCE]; INFRA-643's in-room check covers a cold write's publish.

A planned stale_room_test case 'room replaced by one lacking a delete the fork holds' was not built: the state is unreachable on current code (CloseRoom flushes before evicting while the write's advisory lock holds pending appends; a failed room refuses loads until it compacts under the same lock; a failure before the append is refused at recordLiveOperation's failure check). The cold-fork case is built and fails a tag that ignores the room instance.
